- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.75) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overestimation, reduce subsequent 3–5 days’ forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- If forecast consistently underestimates true values in 30-day horizon, especially after 1–2 positive sentiment days, add 0.5–1.5% to next forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.50) and forecast is significantly below true, assume low volatility and increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid underreaction.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves when sentiment is positive — if forecast drops below 10% of recent 5-day high, flag for correction.
